distinctness: The candidate fails to establish a distinct security vulnerability. It is fundamentally an observation of an arbitrary heuristic thresholding bug (softmax/max-normalization heuristic) conflated with standard action-sampling sensitivity and batch normalization artifacts. The mechanism requires no model inversion, latent adversarial perturbation, or world-model exploitation; it is simply the deterministic arithmetic consequence of evaluating `qvals / qvals.max() > gamma` over a static grid.
fatal_flaws: Implementation artifact vs. principled threat: The deployed mechanism lacks any formal Control Barrier Function (CBF) guarantees, Hamilton-Jacobi reachability analysis, or QP-based safety filtering (as admitted in the source facts). Attacking an ad-hoc heuristic (`dec = qvals / max(qvals)`) is analyzing a trivial software defect, not an architectural vulnerability in world models or latent CBFs.

Tautological vulnerability: Any metric defined strictly relative to the sample maximum will shift its acceptance region if the sample maximum changes. Packaging this elementary property of division-by-maximum as a novel 'relative-reference bypass' is marketing trivial arithmetic as a deep ML security vulnerability.

Conflation with ordinary critic poisoning/distribution shift: If the attacker steers trajectory collection to depress the critic's evaluated maximum, this is standard offline critic manipulation/out-of-distribution value degradation, not a novel latent safety vulnerability.
short_pilot: Freeze the Dreamer world model and critic weights. Construct a synthetic 1D action grid where action a_unsafe has fixed critic value Q(a_unsafe) = 2.0. In Condition A, populate the remaining 25 actions with values Q in [0, 10] (max = 10, dec = 0.2 -> rejected for gamma=0.5). In Condition B, insert or steer candidate actions such that all Q in [0, 2.5] (max = 2.5, dec = 0.8 -> accepted for gamma=0.5). If this trivial algebraic shift accounts for 100% of the safety bypass without altering any latent dynamics or world-model rollouts, the phenomenon is falsified as a safety filter vulnerability and confirmed as a code-level heuristic bug.
repair_assessment: The proposed repair (absolute calibrated thresholding or unnormalized CBF condition) confirms the rejection: replacing `qvals / qvals.max() > gamma` with `qvals > threshold` or standard barrier conditions `dot(B) + alpha(B) >= 0` completely erases the phenomenon, demonstrating that the attack targets an unprincipled implementation choice rather than a fundamental property of latent safety filters.
